source_read: PMC full text PMC5984096 (publisher version, Molecular Psychiatry 23(5):1287-1292, online 24 Jan 2017, CC BY; not an author manuscript), all sections and Figures 1-4 legends, read in the built-in browser in my own tab on 2026-10-27; figure images not inspected (values taken from text and legends); Supplementary Information (methods for the users-vs-non-users rescaling, F statistics, Tables S1-S7, Figs S1-S10) not read

claims.overstatement: None for the figures attributed to this source: 1.08 (1.02-1.14) per unit of log odds of ever use, the authors' rescaling to 1.37 (1.09-1.67) users vs non-users, and 1.41 (1.09-1.83) from the multivariable MR adjusted for the variants' associations with ever smoking all match, with the right exposure (genetic liability to ever use; ICC 10 lead SNPs) and outcome (schizophrenia, PGC). The claim rightly attributes the rescaling to the authors; it is not an editors' calculation. Omissions: the 10 variants did not reach genome-wide significance (p 4.6 x 10^-7 to 3.1 x 10^-6), and the authors' own reading (the genetic approach 'strongly supports' a causal relation) is not reported, although the claim reports the narrative reviews' readings; the claim's headline ('evidence is insufficient') is the editors' synthesis, which this source's authors do not share, and status 'contested' covers this only if the authors' view is named.
claims.note: Instrument strength: the 10 SNPs explain 1% of variance in ever use (Results), matching 'about 1% or less'; F statistics only in the supplement; the authors report I2 = 67% for MR-Egger (potential relative bias 43%) and therefore applied simulation extrapolation (results only in Supplementary Table S7). Sensitivity analyses for other pathways: MR-Egger gave no evidence of directional pleiotropy (p = 0.292; its estimate is not given in the main text), weighted median similar but less precise (no number in the main text), leave-one-out largely unchanged, no outlier SNP, two SNPs with marginal influence; two putatively functional SNPs (KCNT2, NCAM1) gave 1.88 (1.00-3.21); the authors concede MR-Egger and weighted median may be underpowered. The rescaling from 1.08 per unit to 1.37 users vs non-users uses schizophrenia risk in the population and its prevalence in people who never used cannabis, described only in the supplement, so it cannot be checked from the main text; by my arithmetic it corresponds to a contrast of about 4.1 units of log odds of ever use (ln 1.37 / ln 1.08), a large extrapolation from a 1%-variance instrument. On the comparable scale, 1.08 per unit is about 1.055 per doubling of the odds, close to Gage et al. 2017's 1.04. Shared data: ICC (Stringer et al. 2016, 32,330 people) for exposure and the public PGC schizophrenia GWAS (34,241 cases, 45,604 controls) for outcome, the same consortia as Gage et al. 2017; overlap between exposure and outcome data under 5%. Supports 'not independent'. Locators of my anchors were refined after step 2 to name the printed sub-subheadings under 'Characteristics of the genetic markers'; places and data unchanged.

anchors.locator: Results > Causal effect of ever use of cannabis on risk of schizophrenia, 1st paragraph; Figure 2 legend
anchors.extracted: 10 SNPs associated with ever use explained 1% of its variance. Fixed-effect (inverse-variance-weighted) MR in 34,241 schizophrenia cases and 45,604 controls: OR 1.08 (95% CI 1.02-1.14) per 1-log-unit increase in ever use of cannabis, p = 0.007; random effects 1.09 (1.02-1.16), p = 0.010.

anchors.locator: Results > Causal effect of ever use of cannabis on risk of schizophrenia, 1st paragraph; Figure 2 and 3 legends; Materials and methods > Statistical analysis, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Using population-based estimates (schizophrenia risk in the population and prevalence of schizophrenia in people who never used cannabis; method in the Supplementary Information), the per-unit estimate was translated to OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.09-1.67) for users vs non-users (a 37% increase in the authors' words); consistent with the observational estimates (heterogeneity chi2 0.23, p = 0.634, schizophrenia only; chi2 0.10, p = 0.755, combined).

anchors.locator: Results > Assessment of pleiotropic effects of the genetic markers, 2nd paragraph; Materials and methods > Sensitivity analyses, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Multivariable MR adjusting the SNP-schizophrenia estimates for the SNPs' associations with ever vs never smoking (UK Biobank, 111,898 people: 51,984 ever smokers, 59,914 never): OR 1.41 (95% CI 1.09-1.83) for users vs non-users; bootstrap SE (10,000 resamples).

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Genetic markers associated with ever use of cannabis, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Instrument: the 10 leading SNPs of the ICC GWAS of lifetime (ever) cannabis use, mostly European ancestry; none reached genome-wide significance (discovery p between 4.6 x 10^-7 and 3.1 x 10^-6); authors rely on directional consistency across contributing studies (Supplementary Table S4).

anchors.locator: Materials and methods > Characteristics of the genetic markers > Strength of instrument and power to detect a causal effect, 2nd to 4th paragraphs; > Assessment of directional pleiotropy, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Exposure and outcome data overlap under 5%; authors argue weak-instrument bias in non-overlapping samples would bias towards the null. Per-SNP and cumulative F statistics computed (values in the supplement only); power to detect the observational magnitude reported as 100% (Supplementary Table S6). MR-Egger: I2 = 67%, potential bias 43%, so Egger estimates adjusted by simulation extrapolation (SIMEX); Egger SE by 10,000 bootstrap resamples.

anchors.locator: Results > Assessment of pleiotropic effects of the genetic markers, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: MR-Egger gave no evidence against the null of no unmeasured pleiotropy (p = 0.292); weighted median MR gave a very similar estimate with less precision; the Egger, SIMEX-adjusted Egger and weighted median estimates are only in Supplementary Table S7 and Figs S4-S5.

anchors.locator: Results > Sensitivity analyses, 1st paragraph; Figure 4 legend
anchors.extracted: Leave-one-out: direction and precision largely unchanged; no SNP an outlier by studentized residuals; Cook's distance showed marginal influence for two SNPs (rs2033867, rs7107977); two putatively functional SNPs (in KCNT2 and NCAM1) gave OR 1.88 (95% CI 1.00-3.21) for users vs non-users.

Limitations stated by the authors: no investigation of quantity, type, route or age at exposure; mechanisms of the variants unknown; SNPs below genome-wide significance; MR-Egger and weighted median may be underpowered to detect directional pleiotropy.

Authors' reading: the genetic approach strongly supports a causal role of cannabis use in schizophrenia, and the finding may inform public-health messages; they call the study the closest approximation to a randomized trial of ever use.

anchors.locator: Results > Observational association between ever use of cannabis and risk of schizophrenia and related disorders, 1st paragraph; Figure 1 legend
anchors.extracted: Authors' own meta-analysis of prospective observational studies of ever vs never use: one study of schizophrenia (Swedish conscripts) OR 1.50 (1.10-2.00); five studies of schizophrenia or related outcomes (schizophreniform disorder, psychotic symptoms; 1,326 cases, 58,263 controls) pooled OR 1.43 (1.19-1.67), I2 = 0%, random effects.

key_findings.note: Overlap below 5% is in the 2nd paragraph under 'Strength of instrument and power to detect a causal effect'.
The note's statement about the case and control numbers printed in Figure 3 was not checked (figure image not seen); the Figure 3 legend says the numbers are shown.

All values come from the Figure 2 image, which I did not see (the browser became unreachable after my reading, and the text and legend give no per-variant values). Needs a targeted check. The editors' pooled 1.08 (1.02-1.14) matches the text.

Text parts confirmed (largely unchanged; no studentized-residual outlier; rs2033867 and rs7107977 marginal by Cook's distance). The numeric leave-one-out range 1.31 (1.04-1.62) to 1.53 (1.16-1.96), and which removal gives the highest, come from the Figure 4 image, not seen: targeted check needed for those numbers.
Finding confirmed from text. The note's per-unit calculation 1.18 (1.00-1.39) uses Figure 2 values, not checked.

Confirmed from text: Swedish conscripts 1.50 (1.10-2.00); pooled 1.43 (1.19-1.67), I2 0%, 1,326 cases, 58,263 controls. The other four study estimates and all study-level counts are from the Figure 1 image, not seen; the card's counts sum exactly to the text's totals (1,326; 58,263), which supports the reading. The text calls the 58,263 'controls'.

reporting_issues.note: Found the ratio-scale symmetry independently in step 1 (0.24 either side of 1.43). Recomputed from the card's Figure 1 values: log-scale inverse-variance pooling 1.45 (1.23-1.71), untransformed 1.43 (1.19-1.67), Q 1.27; same as the card. The Figure 1 values themselves were not seen.
Recomputed: log-scale SE 0.109; power to detect OR 1.43 at two-sided 0.05 about 0.91.
Under the usual reading of I2_GX, 67% implies about 33% dilution, not 43%.
Flagged independently in step 1 (rs7107977 in this text, rs7107987 in Gage et al. 2017, Table 1). Ratio 0.01/0.27 gives a per-unit OR of about 1.04, consistent with the card's reading.

risk_of_bias.note: High overall: ten sub-threshold variants explaining 1%; exclusion restriction examined for ever smoking only; reverse direction untested; Egger estimates only in the supplement, with a diluted Egger (I2 67%). Editors' F of about 33 recomputed (32.6); per-variant chi-squares 21.8 to 25.4 recomputed.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: 'strongly supports' a causal relation and 'closest approximation to a randomized trial' from a 1%-variance, sub-threshold instrument, with the reverse direction untested and a headline that depends on a rescaling given only in the supplement.

missed: Abstract: P = 0.007 is printed next to the rescaled users-vs-non-users OR 1.37; it is the p-value of the per-unit estimate (1.08), and the abstract describes the rescaled figure as if two groups had been compared directly.

By my arithmetic the rescaling from 1.08 per unit to 1.37 corresponds to a contrast of about 4.1 units in the log odds of ever use (ln 1.37 / ln 1.08), for example roughly from a 5% to a 75% probability (4.04 units) of ever use, which shows how far the headline extrapolates from the per-unit estimate (editors' calculation; the supplement's inputs were not read).
